challenges.headline: Automatic 'manager away' detection
challenges.premise: The system will automatically know a manager is away, presumably from their own approved leave record.
challenges.alternative: A manual flag or a named delegate (set by the manager or HR in advance) avoids wiring one employee's leave approval into the trigger for another employee's workflow.
challenges.consequence: Automatic detection creates a live cross-entity dependency: a manager's own absence record becomes a hidden trigger for other people's approvals, and any staleness or ambiguity in that record (partial day off, pending-not-yet-approved leave) misfires the escalation.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm with the business whether detection must be automatic or whether a manual/delegate-based trigger is acceptable before designing the dependency.

challenges.headline: Undefined escalation target
challenges.premise: The request assumes escalation has an implicit, single destination.
challenges.alternative: An explicit named delegate, the manager's manager, or a per-client configurable target are three different answers, and approval circuits on this platform are already client-specific.
challenges.consequence: Hardcoding one target now risks a rebuild later if even one client needs a different escalation rule — a pattern the platform already has for other approval circuits.
challenges.recommendation: Settle the escalation target and whether it must be configurable per client/country before estimating the build.

challenges.headline: Race: late approval vs. escalation
challenges.premise: The request doesn't address what happens if the original manager approves right after escalation has already fired.
challenges.alternative: A defined precedence rule — e.g. first decision wins and the request locks, or the escalated approver's decision always takes precedence once fired — removes the ambiguity rather than leaving it to runtime behavior.
challenges.consequence: Without this rule, two approvers can both act on the same request, producing conflicting states and a support ticket, not just an edge case.
challenges.recommendation: Define and test the precedence rule explicitly as part of the workflow spec, not as an afterthought.

challenges.headline: Automatic 'away' detection assumed
challenges.premise: The system should automatically detect that a manager is 'away' and trigger escalation.
challenges.alternative: A simpler manual mechanism — the manager (or an admin) pre-designates a delegate before leaving, or sets an explicit out-of-office status — avoids building a timeout/absence-linkage detector for a first version.
challenges.consequence: Automatic detection tied to a timeout or to the absence module is a meaningfully bigger build (polling vs event subscription, false positives, race conditions) than a manually declared delegate, and the request doesn't establish that the bigger version is actually needed.
challenges.recommendation: Validate with the client whether a manually-set delegate/away-flag would solve the real pain before committing to automatic detection.

challenges.headline: Single-hop escalation assumed sufficient
challenges.premise: Escalating to 'another approver' resolves the stall.
challenges.alternative: Defining a guaranteed backstop approver (e.g., HR or a skip-level role) that the chain always terminates at avoids an unresolved request if the escalated approver is also unavailable.
challenges.consequence: Without a defined endpoint, the same stall can simply recur one level up, and the feature fails in exactly the scenario it was built to prevent.
challenges.recommendation: Define a terminal approver for the escalation chain before building the routing logic.

challenges.headline: Balance/quota check left implicit
challenges.premise: The request focuses only on escalation, leaving the balance/quota check that normally accompanies leave approval unaddressed.
challenges.alternative: Explicitly scoping whether this approval step also validates the employee's leave balance avoids silently inheriting (or silently dropping) quota logic that the platform treats as standard on this entity.
challenges.consequence: If the quota check is assumed to exist but isn't rebuilt or reconnected for the escalated path, leave could be approved outside the balance rules the rest of the platform enforces.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm explicitly whether quota validation applies on the escalated approval path, not just the manager's.
